subtopic: Polar Coordinates
stem: Find the Cartesian co-ordinates of the point whose polar co-ordinates are \(\left(2, \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\).
solution:
Given \(r = 2\) and \(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\).
Using \(x = r\cos\theta\) and \(y = r\sin\theta\), we get
\(x = 2\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4} = 2 \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}\) and \(y = 2\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4} = 2 \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}\).
The required Cartesian co-ordinates are \(\left(\sqrt{2}, \sqrt{2}\right)\).

subtopic: Polar Coordinates
stem: Find the polar co-ordinates of the point whose Cartesian co-ordinates are \(\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, \dfrac{-1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\).
solution:
From the co-ordinates of the given point we observe that the point lies in the fourth quadrant.
\(r^2 = x^2 + y^2 = \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 + \left(-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} = 1\), so \(r = 1\).
Since \(x = r\cos\theta\) and \(y = r\sin\theta\), \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 1 \times \cos\theta\) and \(-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 1 \times \sin\theta\).
Hence \(\cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) and \(\sin\theta = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), so \(\theta = \dfrac{7\pi}{4}\).
The required polar co-ordinates are \(\left(1, \dfrac{7\pi}{4}\right)\).

subtopic: Solution of Triangle — Sine, Cosine and Projection Rules
stem: In \(\triangle ABC\), if \(A = 30^\circ\), \(B = 60^\circ\) then find the ratio of sides.
solution:
To find \(a : b : c\). Given \(A = 30^\circ\), \(B = 60^\circ\).
As \(A, B, C\) are angles of the triangle, \(A + B + C = 180^\circ\), so \(C = 90^\circ\).
By Sine rule, \(\dfrac{a}{\sin A} = \dfrac{b}{\sin B} = \dfrac{c}{\sin C}\).
\(\therefore \dfrac{a}{\sin 30^\circ} = \dfrac{b}{\sin 60^\circ} = \dfrac{c}{\sin 90^\circ}\), i.e. \(\dfrac{a}{\tfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{b}{\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} = \dfrac{c}{1}\).
\(\therefore a : b : c = \dfrac{1}{2} : \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} : 1 = 1 : \sqrt{3} : 2\).

subtopic: Solution of Triangle — Sine, Cosine and Projection Rules
stem: In \(\triangle ABC\), if \(a = 2\), \(b = 3\) and \(\sin A = \dfrac{2}{3}\) then find \(B\).
solution:
By sine rule, \(\dfrac{a}{\sin A} = \dfrac{b}{\sin B}\).
\(\therefore \dfrac{2}{\tfrac{2}{3}} = \dfrac{3}{\sin B}\), which gives \(\sin B = 1\).
\(\therefore B = 90^\circ = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\).

subtopic: Solution of Triangle — Sine, Cosine and Projection Rules
stem: In \(\triangle ABC\), prove that \(a(\sin B - \sin C) + b(\sin C - \sin A) + c(\sin A - \sin B) = 0\).
solution:
L.H.S. \(= a(\sin B - \sin C) + b(\sin C - \sin A) + c(\sin A - \sin B)\)
\(= a\sin B - a\sin C + b\sin C - b\sin A + c\sin A - c\sin B\)
\(= (a\sin B - b\sin A) + (b\sin C - c\sin B) + (c\sin A - a\sin C)\).
By the sine rule each bracket is zero (\(a\sin B = b\sin A\), \(b\sin C = c\sin B\), \(c\sin A = a\sin C\)).
\(= 0 + 0 + 0 = 0 = \) R.H.S.

subtopic: Solution of Triangle — Sine, Cosine and Projection Rules
stem: In \(\triangle ABC\), prove that \((a - b)\sin C + (b - c)\sin A + (c - a)\sin B = 0\).
solution:
L.H.S. \(= (a - b)\sin C + (b - c)\sin A + (c - a)\sin B\)
\(= (a\sin C - b\sin C) + (b\sin A - c\sin A) + (c\sin B - a\sin B)\)
\(= (a\sin C - c\sin A) + (b\sin A - a\sin B) + (c\sin B - b\sin C)\).
By the sine rule each bracket is zero.
\(= 0 + 0 + 0 = 0 = \) R.H.S.

subtopic: Solution of Triangle — Sine, Cosine and Projection Rules
stem: In \(\triangle ABC\), if \(a = 2\), \(b = 3\), \(c = 4\) then prove that the triangle is obtuse angled.
solution:
We know that the angle opposite to the largest side of a triangle is the largest angle of the triangle.
Here side \(AB\) (\(= c\)) is the largest side, so \(C\) is the largest angle. We show \(C\) is obtuse.
\(\cos C = \dfrac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2ab} = \dfrac{2^2 + 3^2 - 4^2}{2(3)(4)} = \dfrac{-3}{24} = -\dfrac{1}{8}\).
As \(\cos C\) is negative, \(C\) is an obtuse angle.
\(\therefore \triangle ABC\) is an obtuse angled triangle.

subtopic: Solution of Triangle — Sine, Cosine and Projection Rules
stem: In \(\triangle ABC\), if \(A = 60^\circ\), \(b = 3\) and \(c = 8\) then find \(a\). Also find the circumradius of the triangle.
solution:
By Cosine rule, \(a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc\cos A\).
\(a^2 = 3^2 + 8^2 - 2(3)(8)\cos 60^\circ = 9 + 64 - 48 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 73 - 24 = 49\).
\(\therefore a = 7\).
Now by sine rule \(\dfrac{a}{\sin A} = 2R\), so \(\dfrac{7}{\sin 60^\circ} = 2R\), i.e. \(\dfrac{7}{\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} = 2R\).
\(\therefore R = \dfrac{7}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{7\sqrt{3}}{3}\).
The circumradius of \(\triangle ABC\) is \(\dfrac{7\sqrt{3}}{3}\).

subtopic: Solution of Triangle — Sine, Cosine and Projection Rules
stem: In \(\triangle ABC\), prove that \((a + b)\cos C + (b + c)\cos A + (c + a)\cos B = a + b + c\).
solution:
L.H.S. \(= (a + b)\cos C + (b + c)\cos A + (c + a)\cos B\)
\(= (a\cos C + b\cos C) + (b\cos A + c\cos A) + (c\cos B + a\cos B)\)
\(= (a\cos C + c\cos A) + (b\cos A + a\cos B) + (c\cos B + b\cos C)\).
By the projection rule, \(a\cos C + c\cos A = b\), \(b\cos A + a\cos B = c\), \(c\cos B + b\cos C = a\).
\(= a + b + c = \) R.H.S.

subtopic: Solution of Triangle — Sine, Cosine and Projection Rules
stem: In \(\triangle ABC\), prove that \(a(\cos C - \cos B) = 2(b - c)\cos^2\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)\).
solution:
By Projection rule, \(a\cos C + c\cos A = b\) and \(a\cos B + b\cos A = c\).
\(\therefore a\cos C = b - c\cos A\) and \(a\cos B = c - b\cos A\).
L.H.S. \(= a(\cos C - \cos B) = a\cos C - a\cos B\)
\(= (b - c\cos A) - (c - b\cos A)\)
\(= b - c\cos A - c + b\cos A\)
\(= (b - c) + (b - c)\cos A\)
\(= (b - c)(1 + \cos A)\)
\(= (b - c) \times 2\cos^2\dfrac{A}{2}\)
\(= 2(b - c)\cos^2\dfrac{A}{2} = \) R.H.S.

subtopic: Solution of Triangle — Sine, Cosine and Projection Rules
stem: Prove the Cosine rule using the Projection rule.
solution:
Given: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(a = b\cos C + c\cos B\), \(b = c\cos A + a\cos C\), \(c = a\cos B + b\cos A\).
Multiply these equations by \(a, b, c\) respectively:
\(a^2 = ab\cos C + ac\cos B\)
\(b^2 = bc\cos A + ab\cos C\)
\(c^2 = ac\cos B + bc\cos A\).
\(a^2 + b^2 - c^2 = (ab\cos C + ac\cos B) + (bc\cos A + ab\cos C) - (ac\cos B + bc\cos A)\)
\(= ab\cos C + ac\cos B + bc\cos A + ab\cos C - ac\cos B - bc\cos A\)
\(= 2ab\cos C\).
\(\therefore a^2 + b^2 - c^2 = 2ab\cos C\), i.e. \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C\).
Similarly we can prove that \(a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc\cos A\) and \(b^2 = c^2 + a^2 - 2ca\cos B\).

subtopic: Applications of Sine, Cosine and Projection Rules
stem: In \(\triangle ABC\), if \(a = 13\), \(b = 14\), \(c = 15\) then find the values of (i) \(\cos A\) (ii) \(\sin\dfrac{A}{2}\) (iii) \(\cos\dfrac{A}{2}\) (iv) \(\tan\dfrac{A}{2}\) (v) \(A(\triangle ABC)\) (vi) \(\sin A\).
solution:
\(s = \dfrac{a + b + c}{2} = \dfrac{13 + 14 + 15}{2} = 21\).
\((s - a) = 21 - 13 = 8\), \((s - b) = 21 - 14 = 7\), \((s - c) = 21 - 15 = 6\).
(i) \(\cos A = \dfrac{b^2 + c^2 - a^2}{2bc} = \dfrac{13^2 + 15^2 - 14^2}{2(13)(15)} = \dfrac{198}{390} = \dfrac{33}{65}\).
(ii) \(\sin\dfrac{A}{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{(s-b)(s-c)}{bc}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{7 \times 6}{14 \times 15}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\).
(iii) \(\cos\dfrac{A}{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{s(s-a)}{bc}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{21 \times 8}{14 \times 15}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\).
(iv) \(\tan\dfrac{A}{2} = \dfrac{\sin\tfrac{A}{2}}{\cos\tfrac{A}{2}} = \dfrac{1/\sqrt{5}}{2/\sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{1}{2}\).
(v) \(A(\triangle ABC) = \sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)} = \sqrt{21 \times 8 \times 7 \times 6} = 84\) sq. unit.
(vi) \(\sin A = 2\sin\dfrac{A}{2}\cos\dfrac{A}{2} = 2 \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \times \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{4}{5}\).

subtopic: Applications of Sine, Cosine and Projection Rules
stem: In \(\triangle ABC\), prove that \(\cot\dfrac{A}{2} + \cot\dfrac{B}{2} + \cot\dfrac{C}{2} = \dfrac{a + b + c}{b + c - a}\cot\dfrac{A}{2}\).
solution:
L.H.S. \(= \cot\dfrac{A}{2} + \cot\dfrac{B}{2} + \cot\dfrac{C}{2} = \dfrac{1}{\tan\tfrac{A}{2}} + \dfrac{1}{\tan\tfrac{B}{2}} + \dfrac{1}{\tan\tfrac{C}{2}}\).
Using \(\tan\dfrac{A}{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{(s-b)(s-c)}{s(s-a)}}\) and similarly for \(B, C\),
\(= \sqrt{\dfrac{s(s-a)}{(s-b)(s-c)}} + \sqrt{\dfrac{s(s-b)}{(s-a)(s-c)}} + \sqrt{\dfrac{s(s-c)}{(s-a)(s-b)}}\)
\(= \sqrt{\dfrac{s(s-a)^2}{(s-b)(s-c)(s-a)}} + \sqrt{\dfrac{s(s-b)^2}{(s-a)(s-c)(s-b)}} + \sqrt{\dfrac{s(s-c)^2}{(s-b)(s-a)(s-c)}}\)
\(= \sqrt{\dfrac{s}{(s-b)(s-a)(s-c)}}\,\{(s-a) + (s-b) + (s-c)\}\)
\(= \sqrt{\dfrac{s}{(s-b)(s-a)(s-c)}}\,\{3s - (a + b + c)\}\)
\(= \sqrt{\dfrac{s}{(s-b)(s-a)(s-c)}}\,\{3s - 2s\}\)
\(= \sqrt{\dfrac{s}{(s-b)(s-a)(s-c)}} \times s\)
\(= \dfrac{2s}{2s - 2a}\sqrt{\dfrac{s(s-a)}{(s-b)(s-c)}}\)
\(= \dfrac{a + b + c}{a + b + c - 2a}\sqrt{\dfrac{s(s-a)}{(s-b)(s-c)}}\)
\(= \dfrac{a + b + c}{b + c - a}\cot\dfrac{A}{2} = \) R.H.S.
